content: MK notes that the rest of Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's letters to Sufi masters date to his exile after 830/1427 and sit among otherwise uncontextualized letters of greeting (nos. 35-47); he takes this to suggest the author is 'massaging' his wider network of Sufis and officials in hope of resolving his situation or getting help while wandering. MK gives as an example letter 35, to Sayyid Muḥammad b. Shaykh Kajujī, shaykh al-islām of Tabriz, written ca. 831-32/1428-29 from Lahijan.
